items.q: MCD is also known as lipoid nephrosis; the epidemiological shares written for it are:
opts: 90% of childhood and 10-15% of adult NS
50% of childhood and 50% of adult NS
10-15% of childhood and 90% of adult NS
75% of childhood and 25% of adult NS
items.exp: AKA lipoid nephrosis; 90% of childhood NS; 10-15% of adult NS. (Book p765)

items.q: The peak age group for MCD and its sex preponderance are:
items.exp: Boys > girls; peak age group: 2-7 yrs. (Book p765)

items.q: Selective proteinuria, losing only albumin & transferrin, is seen in few cases of MCD; the bullet for MCD proteinuria in general reads:
items.exp: MCD bullet: non-selective proteinuria; selective (albumin & transferrin only) in few cases. (Book p765)

items.q: The podocyte changes in MCD are effacement of foot process with ↑ CD80 expression and ↑ angiopoietin-like 4 peptide, causing:
opts: Loss of negative charges → leaking of proteins
items.exp: ↑ CD80 and ↑ angiopoietin like 4 peptide → loss of negative charges → leaking of proteins. (Book p765)

items.q: Fill up: In MCD the podocyte surface molecule whose expression rises, alongside angiopoietin-like 4 peptide, is ______.
Two-thirds of MCD relapses follow URTI/LRTI; the relapse-prevention Rx written at onset of URTI/LRTI is:
items.exp: Relapse 2/3rd d/t URTI/LRTI; Rx: prednisolone (0.5 mg/kg) at onset of URTI/LRTI. (Book p765)

items.q: After 4 weeks of steroids, the steroid-resistance share that triggers a biopsy to r/o FSGS is:
items.exp: 5-10% resistance → biopsy taken to r/o FSGS (can cause CKD). (Book p765)

items.q: Among steroid responders, the flowchart splits into 25% cured with no relapse, 25% infrequent relapse (steroid & taper off) and:
opts: 50% FRNS (≥2 relapse in 6 months, ≥4 in 1 year)
items.exp: Respond to steroids: 25% cured, 25% infrequent relapse, 50% FRNS (≥2 in 6 months, ≥4 in 1 year). (Book p765)

items.q: FRNS is started on steroid-sparing agents; the preferred one written is:
items.exp: FRNS: steroid sparing agents: oral cyclophosphamide (preferred). (Book p765)

items.q: SDNS (≥2 relapses within 14 days of stopping steroid or while tapering) is treated with the agent labelled best, which is:
items.exp: SDNS treated using: MMF (best); rituximab. (Book p765)

items.q: In the resistant arm, a normal biopsy may still miss FSGS; genetic studies then decide, with a normal result starting CNI and a positive FSGS result leading to:
items.exp: Normal (sometimes FSGS can be missed) → genetic studies; normal → CNI; FSGS → transplant. (Book p765)
